author: phylliswebb19987
desc: Why It Sucks to Be a Concubine (in Ancient Egypt)#Concubine #animation
transcript: Afterward, you lie on a cedar scented mat and stare at the ceiling where a painted hunting scene loops in bright color. You find the cat in the painting and you stare at it until morning. You decide not to think too much. Thinking too much will only open something you cannot close. Days become weeks. Weeks become a pattern. You learn the pattern and you keep your face smooth. The older women say a smooth face is your greatest tool. They say this without pity, which is almost its own kind of pity. Then one morning, you cannot eat the bread. Your stomach turns at the smell of the oil. The mistress of the household watches your face over her clipboard of accounts. She sends for a physician. He is a priest doctor who smells of natron and old incense. He presses your wrist, checks your eyes, asks you questions in that flat, professional voice. He tells the mistress something in a low tone. The mistress nods. You are pregnant. The house shifts around you like a current changing direction. Your food portions double. A servant is assigned to walk with you in the garden. Mornings and evenings the lady of the house visits your chamber, which she has never done before. She stands in the doorway and looks at your stomach with an expression that is not quite hatred and not quite grief, but lives somewhere in between them. Then she leaves without speaking. That look will live. In you longer than the visit. You ask your mother in your mind, to put her hands on you. She doesn't answer because she is 100 miles south and doesn't know where you are.

author: _baddlad_
transcript: Evil people drank beer for breakfast. They slept in the same bed as their cows. They ran to churches to hide from the law. They ate tree bark when the food was gone. And they burned entire streets full of herbs to fight the Black Death. Still, half of Europe died anyway. This is how the other half stayed alive. Medieval life had one job. Do not die. Sickness could get you. The cold could get you. Hunger could get you wolves, wars, other people. The average peasant lived to about 40 years old. And that was on a good day. So they built survival tricks for everything. Some were smart, some were insane. Most did not work. But every trick started somewhere. And this one started with the thing they drank every morning. Method one beer for breakfast. Medieval water tried to kill you. Rivers were full of animal waste. Wells were dirty. So they drank beer. Not strong beer, weak beer. They called it small ale. It had less alcohol than a soda has sugar. Men drank it, women drank it, kids drank it. A five year old had a mug of beer with his bread at breakfast. The whole village was a little bit drunk all the time. And this was the smart choice. The beer had been boiled. Boiled water is safe water. They did not know why. They just knew. People who drank the beer lived longer. Remember the beer we will come back to It. Water was one problem. The cold was worse. Method 2. They slept with the animals. Medieval winters killed people. Peasant houses had one room, no heater, no warm blankets like we have. So they slept with the animals. The cow slept inside the house. So did the pig. So did the goat. So did the chickens. They were not pets. There were heaters. A cow makes a lot of body heat. Two cows make more. Add a pig and a goat and the room gets warm. Humans on one side, animals on the other. A small wall between them, sometimes not even a wall. It smelled bad. There were fleas. It worked. They also wore the animals sheepskin coats with the wool still greasy inside. The grease made the coat waterproof. They smelled like a dying goat. They did not care. But being warm did not fill an empty stomach. What they ate next, it's worse. Method 3. The pot that never died. There was one pot in every house. It sat over the fire all day, every day. They called it porridge. It was a soup made of anything they had. Turnips, oats, old bread, a carrot. If they were lucky, a piece of meat. If they were unlucky, a piece of squirrel. Here is the important part. They never emptied it. They just kept adding new food on top of the old food. For weeks, sometimes for months. Your dinner tonight was your grandma's lunch from last Tuesday. The bottom of the pot was a mystery nobody wanted to solve. But it was hot, it was food, and it kept them alive. The pot worked for normal life. But normal life did not last. Next came the thing that killed half of Europe. Method 4. The plague. Doctors. In the year 1347, a sickness came to Europe. It was called the Black Death. It killed one out of every two people. In some cities, more. Nobody knew how it spread. They thought sickness came from bad smells. And the cities smelled very bad. So they had a plan. Fight the bad smells with good smells. They burned herbs in the streets. Rosemary, Juniper, whole piles of dried plants. Day and night on every corner. Whole streets full of smoke. Rich people carried small metal balls filled with dried flowers and spices. They held them under their nose in public. Every doctor's cure had strong smells in it. Vinegar, garlic, burned wood. Imagine walking through a city. Smoke everywhere. Herbs burning on every corner. Behind the smoke, people dying in the houses. None of it worked. The plague was not in the smell. The plague was in the fleas, on the rats. But there was one part of plague survival that did work. Rich families ran to the countryside as fast as they could. The people who ran lived. The people who stayed mostly did not. So the real medieval plague medicine was one word run. You could Run from the plague. You could not run from hunger. Method 5. Bark, bread and boiled leather. Sometimes the harvest failed. Not a little, all of it. Two years in a row. This happened in the year 1315. Historians call it the Great Famine. When the food ran out, medieval people ate other things. They ate the bark from trees. They ground it into powder and made bread. It tasted like wood because it was wood. They ate acorns. Acorns are poison. So they soak them for days to remove the poison. Then they ground them into flour.

author: sectorbeta
desc: Thibault, a Young Man left forgotten at the bottom of a well in a medieval castle. #history #curiosity #horrorstories #middleages #animation
transcript: In the Middle Ages, there was a punishment worse than any execution, being thrown into a pit and forgotten forever. In some castles, this prison was hidden beneath the floor. It was a narrow stone shaft, and the only way out was an iron trap door high above. Whoever went down there never saw daylight again. According to legend, this was the fate of Thibo, a young squire serving in a castle in southern France in 1347. One night, the lord's signet ring vanished. Thibo was the only one who had entered his chamber that day. The next morning, the guards dragged him into the Great Hall and pulled back the rug. Beneath it lay an iron hatch with a rusted ring. When they opened it, cold, damp air rose from the darkness. Thibo didn't cry. He simply looked at the Lord of the castle and asked for how long. The Lord adjusted his cloak and replied, until I remember you. They pushed Tibo in. There was the thought of his fall, and then the hatch slammed shut. At first, they lowered bread and water on a rope once a day, and every time the trap door opened, the same voice rose from below. What day is it? No one ever answered. On the 31st day, the Lord gave a new order. No one was to open that hatch again. The rope was pulled up for the last time. The rug was laid back in place. Not long after, a Maid found the lord's ring behind a chest in his own chamber. She ran to tell him. The Lord took the ring, slipped it onto his finger and ordered her to keep quiet. From that day on, she never crossed the middle of the hall again. She walked along the walls and avoided the rug. The other maids laughed at her until the night one of them stepped right on top of the hatch and felt something beneath her feet. A knock, then another and another, slow, always the same rhythm every single day, like someone counting. The trap door was never opened again. The years passed. The Lord was gone. The castle changed hands, and Taylor's story became nothing more than a rumor whispered by the fireplace. Until in 1889, during renovations, workers pulled up the hall's old floor and found an iron hatch sealed shut with rust. It took three men to pry it open. Below was a stone shaft barely wider than a man. Lying down at the bottom among scraps of cloth lay a skeleton curled up against the wall. One of the workers climbed down with a lantern and saw that the walls were covered in scratches. There were hundreds of marks in groups of five. Climbing the stone as high as an arm could reach, he counted more than 400 marks, 400 days. But Teebo had only been fed for 31. The last marks grew fainter and fainter until the final one could barely Be seen just below it, carved deep into the stone, as if with every last bit of strength he had left was a name, Thibo. The Lord of the castle wanted him forgotten. More than 600 years later, we still know his name.

author: redditrecaps.real
transcript: The treehouse from Dark Rider 88. Halloween was always my favorite holiday growing up. Dressing up, eating candy, pulling pranks. What's not to love? But ever since that one Halloween night when I was 12 years old, I've never looked at October 31st the same way again. I grew up in a quiet suburb of Denver, full of families and kids my age. My parents had moved there when I was young because it seemed like such a safe, friendly neighborhood. And it was, for the most part. But maybe nowhere is totally safe from the darker side of things. Anyway. Halloween was a big deal in our community. Everyone would decorate their houses, and kids would spend weeks picking out costumes and planning trick or treat routes to hit the best candy spots. My friends and I loved sorting through our halls after a long night knocking on doors. I had two best friends who lived on my block, Josh and Tyler. One year when we were 12, on Halloween afternoon, we hung out in the treehouse in my backyard, planning out our costumes and strategies for that night. We were going to go as the Ghostbusters crew, complete with homemade proton packs my dad helped us build. We could barely contain our excitement as we helped each other with our costumes before heading out around dusk. It was the perfect night, just chilly enough to warrant a jacket. Clear skies and a bright moon. Josh, Tyler, and I set Out! With our parents trailing behind to supervise, we made our way up and down the neighborhood streets, ringing doorbells and yelling the usual trick or treat at each house. Things were going great. Our bags were loaded up with candy in no time. After a couple hours, we were ready to call it quits. Josh and Tyler came back to my house so we could go through our halls together. We dumped out all the goods on the floor of the treehouse and started sorting it into piles. Chocolate, fruity candy, and salty snacks. We were deep in trading negotiations when Tyler said he had to pee. The restrooms were all the way inside, so he said he just ducked behind a tree at the back of the yard. Josh and I went back to swapping candy as we waited. A couple minutes passed and Tyler still wasn't back. Josh and I joked that maybe he fell in, but when it had been over five minutes, we started to get worried. The tree Tyler went behind was only like 20 feet from the treehouse. There's no way using the bathroom would take this long. Josh and I climbed down from the treehouse and slowly walked toward where we last saw Tyler head. As we made our way across the lawn, the wind picked up, scattering leaves at our feet. The moon above was obscured by clouds passing in front of it. We were halfway to the tree when a Blood curdling scream pierced the night. It sounded like Tyler, but twisted and raw in a way I'd never heard before. Josh and I froze, staring wide eyed at each other. Then we heard it again. That awful, guttural scream coming from the dark shape of the tree. We ran inside, yelling for our parents. My dad and Josh's mom came sprinting out. We were crying, trying to explain what we heard. The adults searched the backyard with flashlights, but found nothing. No sign of Tyler or whatever made that horrifying sound. Josh's mom ran to Tyler's house while my dad called 9 1 1. The police showed up, but also found no trace of him. Needless to say, trick or treating was over for the night. Josh's mom stayed with us as we all anxiously awaited news. Around midnight, a knock finally came at the door. It was Tyler, escorted by a police officer. He looked completely normal, not scared or hurt at all. When we asked what happened, he seemed confused. Tyler said he just went to pee behind the tree and came right back. But we weren't in the treehouse anymore. He assumed we went inside without him. Of course, we were incredulous. There's no way Tyler could have made it back to the treehouse without us seeing him in that tiny backyard. And we definitely heard those screams that sounded just like him. Tyler insisted he never screamed and that he just took a quick pee. Break! Our parents were disturbed and relieved at the same time. We were all sufficiently freaked out, so Tyler just went home after that. I slept with the covers over my head that night, listening for any screams from outside my window, but none came. The next day, things felt relatively back to normal. We still had fun trading candy and telling ghost stories like any other post Halloween. But there was an unspoken unease whenever we made eye contact. Each of us knew what we heard and that it didn't come from our friend. Tyler moved away the next year, and Josh and I drifted apart in high school, but we've never spoken about that night again. I haven't been trick or treating since. Even now, in my 20s, I get anxious as soon as the sun starts going down on Halloween. These days, shadows seem to move in a way they shouldn't, carrying whispers of the unexplained. Whatever terrifying presence visited my backyard that night, I don't intend to encounter it ever again.

transcript: Union Cannonball crashes through the kitchen and lands in Wilmer's fireplace. As most sensible people would, he looks at the gaping hole in his kitchen wall, looks back at the Cannonball, and starts to think, you know, this war thing ain't for me. At the time, he had no idea that the cannonball he was staring at was the first shot fired of the American Civil War at what would be later known as the battle of Bull Run. Wilmer decides to do the best thing he can do to get away from the fighting. He purchases a property roughly 120 miles south in another part of Virginia and hits the road with his family. They travel for days, each mile feeling a little safer and just that little bit farther from a war that found its way to his doorstep. They move into their new home, and finally, they're safe for now. The war that everyone thought was going to be a quickie drags on and becomes the bloodiest conflict in American history. Four years pass, and though they had won many of the initial conflicts in the war, by 1865, the Confederacy was hanging on by a thread. In April of that year, Confederate general Robert E. Lee is being pursued by union troops LED by Ulysses S. Grant. Reached the town of Appomattox, Virginia, starving, having marched without food for days. Hoping for just a moment to catch their breath. They're almost immediately found by Grant's men, who Surround them outside the town courthouse, General Lee realizes that the game is up. Rather than send his men to die, he decides to surrender. He looks around the town for a nice house that would be a suitable place to end the war. They find one to their liking, and Lee and grant approach the house together and knock on the door. You gotta be fucking kidding me. The two generals ask Wilmer if they can use his living room to sign the documents that would certify General Lee surrender. He reluctantly agrees, and his home is once again filled with Civil War troops. At least nothing comes crashing through the wall this time. But maybe it's even worse. See many of the men standing in Wilmer's living room.

author: palaceintrigue1
transcript: People said women with wide hips were born to bear heirs. They were destined to become empress. Before leaving for war, father held mother's hand. He told her clearly, have Nanan learn dance. Three years later, I would enter the palace selection. Mother nodded through her tears. The next day, she hired a martial arts master. I was stunned. Mother, didn't father say dance? Mother said yes, martial arts will keep you alive. Three years later, I was covered in muscle. I could draw a heavy war bow. I could split a thick wooden post with 1 slash. On selection day, the examiner asked us to show our talents. The girls before me recited poems, painted and danced. They were all graceful and delicate. When it was my turn, I grabbed a bronze cauldron and lifted it one handed. The emperor froze, then declared, this girl has outstanding skill. He made me a 6th rank armed guard, shocking the whole hall. I froze. A guard? An armed guard. Didn't mother say the selection was to become the emperor's wife? How did I become his bodyguard? I turned to stone as mother grabbed my hand. She was overjoyed. Nanan, did you hear that his Majesty values you? 6th rank right from the start? Your father worked 10 years to reach 6th rank. I looked at mother. She was truly happy. She was also truly proud. But I knew this was not how it was supposed to go. Father's plan had gone Off track. Half a month later, father returned victorious. He had just entered the city, still in armour. Mother and I hurried forward to greet him. Father smiled when he saw us. Mother said, my Lord, you're finally back. I have wonderful news for you. Father asked, did Nanan make something of herself? He patted mother's back and looked over at me. How did Nanan selection go? Did his Majesty keep her token? Mother smiled. He did more than that. His Majesty issued an edict and gave Nanan an official post. Father froze. How can a concubine hold office? His Majesty said Nanan's martial skill is exceptional. He named her a 6th rank armed guard. Father's smile stiffened. Martial skill, an armed guard? Mother nodded, yes. Thanks to your advice back then, I hired the best martial arts master for Nana. Now she can draw a heavy war bow. Father cried out in grief, got overwhelmed and fainted on the spot. Late that night, father woke up at home, pale as paper. He pointed at me in my guard uniform, trembling with rage. You unfilial girl. I wanted you in the harem living comfortably. Why are you blocking blades for the emperor? The palace is a deadly den. Chancellor Wei Wu Ji is even more treacherous. What if you get dragged into power struggles and die? Seeing him about to pass out again, I quickly promised father, don't worry, I won't cause trouble. I'll stay alive and stay away from Wei Wu Ji palace schemes, open fights, power grabs. As long as they don't block my pay, I won't see a thing. I'll keep a low profile and collect my salary. I absolutely won't stir up trouble. Father stared at my unlucky money saving face. His grand political plan shattered completely. In the end, he could only sigh. The next day, I put on my guard uniform and reported for duty outside Zichen Hall. Emperor Xiao Jingchen stood with his hands behind his back. Seeing my straight posture, suspicion flashed in his eyes. He was naturally paranoid and he had chosen me during the selection. He had taken a liking to my brute strength. He could use me to disrupt the noble family's plans. But now that I was truly by his side, the more he thought, the stranger it felt. Because of court rumors, he suspected the Shen family had ties to the chancellor. Now, the Shen family had not sent him a delicate beauty. They had sent a monster who could uproot a Willow tree. How could a noble lady have such terrifying skills? He knew Way Wu Ji kept elite assassins under his command. Maybe General Shen was proving loyalty by working with Way Wu Ji. Maybe they had staged this entire swap. The girl before him might not be the real Shen daughter. She might be the Chancellor's top assassin, and she had been sent right under his nose to test me, Xiao Jingchen decided to Use the chancellor's secret signal, he would hit me with a serious test himself. Late that night, I leaned against a dragon pillar calculating food costs. A dark figure crept over like a giant rat. It was Yao Jingchen's trusted eunuch. He disguised himself as the chancellor's contact and came up masked. He shoved a 50 tail gold ingot into my hand. Then he winked wildly and made the chancellor's hand signals. He stuck out his backside like he was holding a giant watermelon. He lowered his voice and gave the code. The king covers the tiger. In the shadows, Xiao Jingchen watched me closely. He had calculated it. If I were an assassin, I would answer and take the gold. If I were another spy, I would draw my blade and alarm. But I stared at the ingot and my mental abacus went crazy. Someone was giving me free money in the middle of the night. I shoved the gold in my mouth and bit a clear row of teeth marks into it. Then I saw him hugging air like a watermelon and it clicked. He had come to Zichen Hall at night to bribe an Imperial guard. This wasn't an assassin. This was easy credit. I slapped him across the face on reflex. Before the unit could finish, he spun three and a half times. His eyes rolled back and he passed out peacefully on the stone floor. I grabbed him by the collar and dragged him into The hall like a chicken. Then I tossed him at Xiao Jing's feet like a sack. Your Majesty, I have an urgent report. This man had crooked eyes, a twisted mouth and kept acting crazy. He was clearly an assassin trying to bribe me. May I count this 50 tiles as this month's bonus? Xiao Jingchen looked at the swollen foaming eunuch on the floor. Then he looked at my sincere face and fell silent. What scheming old fox would raise an idiot who sold out a contact for 50 tails? By dumb luck, I passed the first test that stung Wei Wu Ji spy inside the palace. That spy was Xiao Xiaotian, commander of the Imperial Guards. Seeing me win favor on day 1, he decided to get rid of me at evening shift change. Xiao Xiaotian blocked my way with his men. Shenwuwei, you're new here and need some training. I put down the apple I was chewing. I cupped my fists. Commander, what are your orders? Do you have a job for me? Yao Xiao Tian gave a fake smile and pointed west. Tonight you guard the Royal Beast Garden. It houses rare beasts. It's a royal site and your strength makes you perfect for it. I frowned at the word night shift. Sir, this is a rough back to back shift. Will there be double night pay? Jiao Xiaotian froze and his men looked at each other. The contempt in his eyes grew deeper. What a Clueless fool still thinking about money before death. Jiao Xiaotian pretended to be generous. Guard it well. I'll report your merit tomorrow and you'll get paid. Hearing there was extra pay, my eyes instantly lit up. Thank you for the promotion. I agreed fast and bowed. Watching me leave happily, Xiao Xiao Tian gave a cold snort. Go up in the man eating black tiger's cage. Tomorrow, collect that guard's bones. Late that night, the Royal Beast Garden was deathly quiet. High walls loomed and beasts growled in the distance. Xiao Xiao Tian had purposely assigned me no partner in the huge garden. I was the only one on duty. I had just found a comfy spot by the rockery. Suddenly, a foul wind hit me and a green eyed black tiger appeared, drooling stinking saliva. It lunged straight at me. Its bloody jaws came right from my face.

author: luckyballleague
desc: The Wooden Ball That Saved a Warship #shorts #history #storytime #animation #engineering
transcript: He chucked a polished wooden ball straight down the boiler pipe of a brand new warship. You see, the royal inspector nearly had a stroke right there on the iron deck. He grabbed the machinist by the collar, screamed, you just sabotaged a 10,000 pound brass engine with a wooden toy. All the rival engineers laughed their heads off. Their engines were masterpieces of gleaming laser. Straight iron flap valves, polished clean enough to see your face in. Then came the full throttle steam test out on open water. Within 20 minutes, sea salt and mineral gunk baked onto those expensive metal flaps. Steel welded to steel. The rival ship's pressure needle pegged past red and kaboom! Steaming iron rivets blasted across the deck like shotgun pellets. Meanwhile, our machinist sat sipping tea. Wait. Wood inside a boiling steam furnace? Well, you see, metal flap valves open on a rigid hinge. Think of a heavy iron bathroom door. Kick a tiny pebble underneath it and the whole thing jams wide open. A floating ball has no hinges. It rolls freely with the rushing current, self centering over the hole every single stroke. It even grinds mineral scale to powder without getting stuck. When the fleet returned to port, the rival engine was a twisted hunk of smoking scrap metal and resting inside the champion pipe.

author: explainedhistory9
transcript: The French quickly destroy all of the bridges over the river and defiantly block Henry's path. He's forced to travel south, trying to find a way to cross, all the while, the food supplies for his army dwindling and dysentery continuing to spread through his ranks. After marching for weeks, Henry finally leads his men across the Somme, miles downstream from where he had originally intended to cross. They had long run out of food and are starving. But at least they're now marching on a path that will take them directly to Calais. But just when Henry thinks he's in the clear, the French army slowly begins to materialize in front of him. One by one, an endless stream of mountain knights ride out and form a line. The swarm of Frenchmen is unending, and eventually the opposing force is so vast, it's clear to everyone that the English are outnumbered at least two to one. Henry turns to look at his men, and they are a sorry sight. They're dirty, tired, sick and starving. In fact, his archers, who by this point were nearly all stricken with dysentery, had removed their pants after growing tired of constantly shitting themselves and were now standing there naked from the waist down like a mob of medieval poo bears. English man in arms looks out at a massive French army and begins to panic. He starts shouting how badly they're outnumbered. Henry turns to his men and quickly replies, I would Not even if I could have a single man more than I do. Do you not believe that the Almighty, with these, his humble few, is able to overcome the arrogance of the French, who boast of their great number and of their strength? He swears to his men that he'll accept no Ransom for his life. If they fall, he will die with them. The words of their king steal the English, and they prepare to fight. Henry quickly sends his accompanying priests to hear the final confessions of all his men, and the French watch from across the battlefield as the English soldiers kneel before the priests and confess their mortal sins. The last of his soldiers crosses himself and stands, and Henry marches his men out onto the battlefield. Both armies lock eyes in silence, neither side willing to make the first move. As the French shift their position, Henry expertly moves his small line to match them. As they jockey for position, the minutes stretch to hours, and soon night falls. The French begin to retreat back to the nearby villages while Henry's men watch them in complete darkness. Suddenly, the sky opens up and freezing rain begins to fall. Henry and his men are quickly soaked to the bone, and they rush to take shelter under the nearby trees. As they listen to the sound of the wind and rain, they stare off into the cold night and see the warmth of the French bonfires. Flickering in the distance, the wind carries sounds of laughing and eating, which makes the men groan in envy. Henry orders his men to maintain complete silence. He announces that anyone who makes a single sound will have their ear cut off. As his men try their best to sleep through the storm, the king and his commanders stay up to carefully plan the battle to come. He's out manned and fighting on enemy soil. Henry knows his plan must be perfect or this miserable night will be the last for everyone here. The sleepless king watches the sunrise and carefully puts on his helmet. A fix to the top is a shining gold crown with the marks of England and France. Like a lighthouse in the dark morning, the sun's rays dance proudly on the shining crown. The king will be unmistakable on the battlefield. He will not hide or command from the rear. He will fight and is prepared to take on anyone who comes at him. Henry mounts a tiny grey horse and rides out onto an area of the battlefield that he's chosen based on his recon missions throughout the night. The rain has turned the field into a thick sea of MUD, and he brings his men to a spot where the forest on both sides of the field narrow in towards him. The king then begins to position his army. He places his men in arms in a thin line in the center. He Positions his archers to each side and has them drive wooden stakes that point outward in front of their line.

desc: Hotel Night Shift Horror Stories Animated 👽🎃👻  #scaryanimatedstories #truehorrorstories #creeptstorytime #animatedstories #horroranimations
transcript: That night, I couldn't sleep. I kept checking the hallway through the peephole in my apartment. It got worse. One Saturday, I saw him on the platform in my train station. He didn't say anything, just stood there at the other end, watching me. I rode three extra stops and walked home on a different day. The next day, I had told my manager, David. He was concerned, but unsure of what to do. He's not a guest here anymore, he said. We could ask him to leave if he shows up again. But unless he threatens you. He paused. I felt helpless, so I started documenting everything. Dates, times, what he said, where I saw them. I kept the gifts as evidence. The final stroll came on a Wednesday afternoon. I was working the desk, and William walked in like he owned the place. Jessica, we need to talk, he said. I stood up. No, we don't. You need to leave. He stepped closer. I care about you. I think you feel the same. My hands were shaking. I picked up the phone and dialed in YPD. I then told him, you need to leave now. He stared at me, stunned. Then he laughed. You're overreacting. No, I said loud and clear. I'm not. Two officers arrived within 10 minutes. William, of course, tried to play it cool, acting like it was all a misunderstanding. But I showed them the log, the notes, the gifts. One officer asked if I wanted to file a report. Yes, I said. They escorted him out. It wasn't dramatic, but it was final. William hasn't come back since. Some nights, I still feel nervous walking home. I still glance over my shoulder. But each day, I feel a little stronger. Working at the front desk, I've Learned how to smile when I don't want to. How to be polite when someone doesn't deserve it. And how to say no when someone crosses the line. Most of all, I've Learned that keeping quiet doesn't keep you safe. Next time, I'll speak up sooner. It's been about a year since I called the police on William. Sometimes it feels like a lifetime ago. Other times, it feels just like last week. I still remember his face. The way he looked at me. Like I was something he owned. That look still shows up in my dreams. But life is better now. A lot better. After everything that happened, I decided I needed a change. I quit my job at the hotel. Three months after the incident. I couldn't sit behind that front desk anymore. Every time the doors opened, I felt a jolt of fear. I'd scan the lobby for him for weeks. I kept expecting him to come back. He never did. But the fear stayed with me. Quiet, heavy. Sitting in my chest like a stone. I moved apartments, too. Nothing fancy. Just a small studio in Queens. I like it there. It's Quieter. And my neighbors are friendly. There's a little grocery store around the corner and a park where I walk in the evenings. It's really peaceful, in a way Manhattan never was. I started seeing a therapist after I moved. At first, I didn't really want to go. I didn't think I needed it. But talking to someone really helped. I realized I was still carrying so much fear, anger, and shame. She told me that none of it was my fault. And I think finally I believe her. I now work at a bookstore. It's a small place, locally owned, with warm lights and shelves that go up to the ceiling. The owner, Dana, is kind and funny, and she treats me like a person, not just an employee. I get to help people find stories they'll love. I get to talk about books, drink tea behind the counter, and feel safe. And I never have to wear a name tag again. Sometimes I think about who I was back then. The girl behind the front desk, trying to stay polite, trying to not cause trouble. I really wish I could go back and tell her that it's really okay to speak up, it's okay to protect yourself. That being nice to someone doesn't mean you owe them anything. I still check over my shoulder when I walk home. I keep my phone in my hand. I double lock my door every night. That part of me might never Go away. I've accepted that. But I'm not scared all the time now. I'm stronger. I'm more careful. Yes, but I'm also more sure of myself. I know what I will and won't allow. I know how to set boundaries. And I know that if anyone ever tries to cross them again, I'll be ready. William took something from me. A sense of ease, maybe a bit of trust in the world. But he didn't take me. I'm still here. I'm still living. And finally, I feel like I'm in control of my own life again.
